units.translation: Or has this long-lived age appeared to the old?
Aged partner of my bed, noble lady.
O aged mother, dear to Xerxes.
I will share my anger with you; for you are older.

Thus G. Burges for γεραφρόνων [of the reverend]. Similar is παλαιόφρων [old-minded] Suppl. 593, Eum. 838, 871. Others have conjectured γεραροφρονῶν [being reverend-minded] or γεραρὰ φρονῶν [thinking reverend thoughts], so that it may correspond more accurately to the strophic verse.
But you, learn from one born late, old-minded one.
After πρεσβυτοδόκοι [receiving the elders] a substantive has fallen out, such as προβούλοις [councillors], which Hermann conjectured.
Loving children and pleasing to the old.
And for the old, the hearths that receive the elders may flourish.
Whoever betrayed your honor to mortals.
Robbing the gods of their honors.
For having given honors to mortals.
He distributes honors to the gods, different ones to different gods.
Who else determined honors for these new gods?
This honor must come from others.
From where will you get the honor of a hand equally feasting?
And upon me is an ancient honor.
So that I might have an honored privilege.
The whole people of the Bactrians is utterly destroyed, not just the old men.
Fallen around the bodies, children of old men.
For the old always flourish in learning well.
You will learn, being an old man, that it is hard for one of your age to be taught.
Go, you and the old men.
And you have come with a wise and faithful old man.
The city will not blame an old man as a messenger.
It is good even for an old man to learn wisdom.
From a loin-aching --- wretched old man.
An ancient saying has been established among mortals.
May old murder no longer breed in the house.
And I somehow taste the ever-living grass.
Of a young woman—who has tasted of a man.

The tragedians use this noun only in the singular, except that Aeschylus once used the dual γαῖν [two lands], as will be said below. γῆ [earth] is used either generally of the earth, whether inhabited and cultivated or not, or specifically of a particular land or city. Examples of both kinds are these.
where I added γᾶς [earth], which was missing in M.
For thus it was corrected in the margin of Askew's copy for ἐν δυοῖν [in two].
Earth is opposed either to the sky or to the sea or to the regions of the underworld, which are said to be κατὰ (or κάτω) γῆς [down under the earth] or ὑπὸ γῆν [beneath the earth].
To the regions of the underworld
